text: I invite businesses to partner us in being catalytic agents to the transition, by moving ahead of the curve to bring about the next bound of sustainability.

speaker: ﻿The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I invite the community to partner us in building a social compact that will make us the greenest generation so far.

speaker: ﻿The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I invite everyone to partner us in building a green nation together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Chairman, let me now elaborate on our vision for a zero-waste nation and my pet topic – no, not smoking, but hawkers and hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Since the launch of the Zero Waste Masterplan in 2019, my Ministry and NEA have taken concrete steps to move from a throwaway culture towards a more sustainable paradigm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are making good progress, addressing our priorities waste streams of electronic waste, or e-waste, packaging waste and food waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked for an update on the e-waste Extended Producer Responsibility, or EPR, scheme that was implemented in July 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These collection points are situated at accessible locations, like community centres and shopping malls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It is a start, but is only a fraction of our collection targets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have done better for large household appliances, with a collection rate of 18%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Together with ALBA, we will roll out extensive publicity and outreach efforts throughout the year, across various marketing and online platforms, focusing on events such as International E-waste Day in October.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: ALBA has also worked with all 17 Town Councils to organise quarterly collection drives at housing estates to collect bulky e-waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On 6 February 2023, I moved the Resource Sustainability (Amendment) Bill for first reading.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There will be a full debate on the Bill during the Second Reading.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Today, I will share more details on two key initiatives under the Bill: a disposable carrier bag charge and a beverage container return scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They are decisive steps to reduce packaging waste and increase recycling, including single-use plastics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: By making the cost of disposable bags visible to consumers, the charge will nudge consumers to be mindful of and reduce their usage of disposable bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Based on NEA's 2021 survey of around 1,000 residents, close to 90% agreed that they had a part to play in reducing the usage of disposable carrier bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: More than 70% also agreed that a mandatory charge will help to reduce the usage of these bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Following consultations with supermarket operators, we understand that the majority will be charging five cents per bag, and this would moderate potential cost impact on consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We can avoid the charge by bringing our own reusable bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The mandatory charge will cover around 400, or about two-thirds, of all supermarket outlets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These include large supermarket chains, such as FairPrice, Cold Storage, Giant and Sheng Siong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These supermarkets will be easily identifiable through collaterals displayed at their premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The mandatory charge would not apply at other retail outlets, such as convenience stores, as suggested by Mr Ng.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Nevertheless, I note that many retailers already charge for bags voluntarily, including large convenience store chains, such as 7-Eleven and Cheers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will monitor the effectiveness of the charge and assess the need to expand the mandatory coverage in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The charge will apply to all disposable carrier bags, not just plastic bags, as all bags require resources and generate carbon emissions during their production and disposal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Other similar schemes in Hong Kong, Taiwan and the UK, have led to a reduction of plastic bags used by 60% to 90%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have heard concerns about supermarket operators profiting from the charge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For transparency and accountability, supermarket operators will be required to publish information on the number of bags issued, amount of proceeds collected and how the proceeds are used.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked how we can balance the charge and the need for bags for waste disposal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The charge will not remove the public's access to disposable bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Bags will still be available at supermarkets and other retail outlets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: By reducing waste and recycling right, we will require fewer bags for waste disposal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Additionally, we can repurpose product packaging to bag waste, including toilet roll bags or packaging from online purchases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, a beverage container return scheme, which Mr Gan mentioned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The scheme is part of an EPR approach to manage packaging waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beverage producers will be responsible for collecting and recycling the products they put to market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Consumers will pay a small deposit when buying a pre-packaged beverage and receive a full refund when the empty beverage container is returned for recycling at a conveniently located return point.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The scheme will cultivate recycling habits and aggregate clean and high-quality recyclables, which can be made into new products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The scheme framework has been developed following extensive stakeholder consultations since 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Around 80% of 1,000 households surveyed in 2021 generally supported implementing the scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Plastic bottles and metal cans comprise about 70% of beverage containers put to market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They are easy to collect, compactible and have high material value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Similar schemes have been implemented in over 50 jurisdictions, such as Norway and Sweden.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Many have seen return rates increase to over 80%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Even as we strengthen legislation to drive behaviour change, we must continue with outreach and education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Prof Koh Lian Pin spoke on The Waste Café.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As noted in my Parliamentary Question reply yesterday, we will take into consideration the views of those who felt that this experiment could have been done differently, to improve our future campaigns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I also thank Prof Koh for his queries on our initiatives to encourage household recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On transparent recycling bins, we will be releasing our findings soon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On recycling chutes, HDB introduced dual chutes for refuse and recyclables for all new public housing developments from 2014.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Since 2018, NEA has also required them at all new non-landed, private residential developments higher than four storeys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In tandem with education campaigns, the E-waste EPR scheme, the upcoming beverage container return scheme and initiatives by other organisations to sort recyclables, such as paper and textiles, will reduce contamination in our blue bins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Members will be heartened to learn that all households can collect a Bloobox from vending machines deployed island-wide later this month, to set up a recycling corner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Designed by a team of students from the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT), the Bloobox is foldable, reusable and light.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It has labels to help households identify what can and cannot be recycled, with reminders that plastic bottles, metal cans and glass containers for recycling should be empty, and free of food and liquids.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Members may pick up a Bloobox from the Parliament Library to start your own recycling corner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I will now speak about our hawker centres and hawker culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our hawker centres are an important institution, providing us with affordable and tasty hawker food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan and Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked about planning considerations for new hawker centres and markets, and the progress of the new hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Pritam Singh also asked about plans for hawker centres in the Marina Bay Financial area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These sites are selected after carefully considering factors, including residential catchment, availability of comparable dining options and complementary facilities in the vicinity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This ensures the centres serves the demand of the residents, while avoiding over competition amongst comparable F&B establishments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Even as we build new centres, we need to ensure that there are hawkers and that they can make a decent livelihood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: CBD hawker centres face additional challenges due to their heavy reliance on the working lunch crowd and the lack of residential catchment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Today, there are already existing food options in the CBD for workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These include four hawker centres such as Market Street Hawker Centre that just reopened last year, as well as about 50 coffeeshops, food courts and canteens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last year, four new hawker centres opened in Senja, Bukit Canberra, Fernvale and Punggol.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Besides Market Street Hawker Centre, another redeveloped centre that commenced operations was Margaret Drive Hawker Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Repairs and Redecoration (R&R works) were also completed at 15 centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Many Singaporeans have explored these centres as part of hawker centre hopping circuits, which is becoming a national pastime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: (In Mandarin):   This year, we can look forward to the opening of two new hawker centres in Buangkok and Woodleigh Village.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Both hawker centres will have around 40 stalls and 700 seats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Both hawker centres will be connected to neighbourhood amenities and transport nodes, making it convenient for residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The seating areas are spacious, family friendly, and inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ceilings are high to ensure better ventilation and airflow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Additionally, the refreshed Jurong West Hawker Centre is slated to reopen in the third quarter of 2023 after the completion of reconfiguration works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: (In English): We are also futureproofing hawker centres through the Hawker Centres Transformation Programme (HTP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As Ms Nadia would be aware, we are piloting the HTP at Cheng San Market and Food Centre and Geylang Serai Market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: NEA will be engaging stallholders before targeting to start works from 2024.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have provided hawkers with a conducive business environment including ensuring reasonable rentals at our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For NEA's monthly tender exercises, we adopt a transparent and fair system with no minimum bid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Individuals can bid for a stall at a monthly rental as low as $1 per month, while others may submit higher bids to secure stalls at popular locations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: After the first three years, rent is adjusted towards assessed market rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In fact, only about 4% of cooked food stalls in hawker centres today are paying rent at above the assessed market rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The remaining over 5,600 stallholders are paying rent no higher than the assessed market rate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, we have also supported hawkers by providing 10 months of rental waiver and six months of subsidies for table cleaning and centralised dish-washing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In fact, stall rentals at hawker centres are generally lower than most other comparable food establishments in their vicinity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Nonetheless, rental only accounts for about 9% of our hawkers' operating costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hawkers price their food based on multiple factors including operating costs, location, business level and patron demographics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They delicately balance these factors to attract patrons while trying to make a decent living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Today, patrons can continue to find affordable options in our hawker centres – as Mr Singh also acknowledges – including the Socially-conscious Enterprise Hawker Centres (SEHCs), where operators have committed to provide at least one budget meal option per stall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To help Singaporeans cope with inflationary pressure, the Government is, among other measures, providing CDC and GST vouchers under the Assurance Package, and with more assistance provided to the lower income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: CDC vouchers can be used at our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government will continue to monitor the situation and consider if further support is needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are taking additional steps to futureproof our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under the Productive Hawker Centres (PHC) Programme, the Hawkers' Productivity Grant (HPG) provides co-funding to purchase kitchen automation and queue management equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam would be happy to know close to $3 million has been provided to more than 900 hawkers under the HPG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Additionally, eight existing centres have tapped on PHC funding to implement centre-level Centralised Dish Washing (CDW) and Automated Tray Return System (ATRS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Today, more than 70% of cooked food stallholders in our hawker centres are already using e-payment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Support groups have been set up at 37 hawker centres to help hawkers embrace digital opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Gan asked what can be done to support hawkers to digitalise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Additionally, we will broaden the ATRS component of the PHC programme to cover Cleaning Process Automation (CPA) solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This helps to address challenges such as ageing cleaners and rising manpower costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Examples include autonomous systems that clean tables and transfer used trays and crockery from tray return points to centralised dishwashing areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Coupled with the mandatory tray and crockery return, these would help to improve the cleanliness situation and bird nuisance issues raised by Ms Nadia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: With everyone doing their part to return their used trays and crockery, we noticed that the situation has generally improved and bird nuisance feedback at hawker centres has been declining annually from 2019 to 2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As we celebrate our veteran hawkers, I am also heartened by the new hawkers who have joined the trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Miss Chan would be happy to hear that many of them have benefited from NEA's Incubation Stall Programme (ISP) and Hawkers' Development Programme (HDP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Together with other similar programmes by our SEHC operators, over 50 aspiring hawkers have joined the hawker trade through these programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As part of our tradition, you would have tried some hawker fare from our ISP and HDP hawkers at yesterday's tea break.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This included delicious halal braised duck kway teow from an ISP stall by Jonathan Tan and Habri Hammad Bin Mohammad at Amoy Street Food Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Johnathan adapted his grandfather's Hokkien braised duck recipe into a halal recipe so the Muslim community can enjoy his food, while continuing his grandfather's legacy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Through feedback, we realised that additional emphasis on culinary readiness alongside close mentorship from hawker mentors will raise participants' chances of success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Therefore, the HDP's classroom programme will spend more time honing culinary skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: At the apprenticeship stage, hawker mentors will also help to assess the participants' culinary readiness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Those selling such snacks usually find it difficult to sustain an entire cooked food stall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will work with SEHCs operators to pilot the use of kiosks, which would incur lower rental and operating cost to support the sale of snacks such as muah chee and putu piring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We hope this will help to preserve these snacks as part of our hawker culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will monitor the viability of such kiosks before deciding if we should scale up this pilot.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Chairman, I am heartened that many Members have called on Singaporeans to embrace sustainability, reduce consumption and green business practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I remember the slogan "Courtesy begins with you and me".

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Minister of State Dr Koh Poh Koon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are making strong efforts to strengthen our resilience on these fronts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Food security is an existential concern for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We import more than 90% of the food we consume, making it impossible for us to insulate ourselves completely from global food supply and price shocks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Over the past two years, we have experienced first-hand the effects of supply chain disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, climate change, geopolitical disruptions and developments elsewhere as well as policy decisions taken by foreign governments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But this does not mean that we are completely at the mercy of such external factors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We can shore up our resilience if we work together as a nation – with Government, industry and consumers each playing our part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about lessons learnt during the COVID-19 pandemic pertaining to food resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak similarly wanted to know how our importers and consumers can become more resilient towards food supply shocks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) will continue to accredit more import sources and facilitate the industry's further diversification through sourcing trips and business networking sessions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Having new sources for food imports will strengthen our resilience but only if the companies put in place robust business continuity plans (BCPs), continue to diversify sources at the company level and maintain warm links with multiple import sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This would help them to pivot more easily when needed and protect their businesses during supply disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak will be happy to note that the industry is adapting and working with SFA to review their BCPs and diversify their supplies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While Singapore imports most of our food and is a price-taker, consumers too can exercise flexibility in their food choices when supply disruptions occur and pivot to other alternatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Last year, we announced the enhancement of our Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund to offer farms a higher co-funding quantum to a wider range of food types such as fruited vegetables and mushrooms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I am glad to announce that SFA will launch the first land tender for this wider range of food types in the later half of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will provide consumers with more food choices that are produced locally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SFA will provide more details when the tender is launched.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To build up even more industry capacity, we will need to optimise our limited agriculture spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are making good progress in master planning Lim Chu Kang, where we will transform the region into a high-tech agri-food zone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We intend to reap synergies between land-based farms in the Lim Chu Kang region and sea-based farming in the adjacent West Johor Strait.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, may I have your permission to display a slide on the LED screens please?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, we are exploring siting our fish hatcheries and other key infrastructural and processing facilities on land, to provide support to both land-based and sea-based fish farms.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will also incorporate upcoming regional studies for coastal protection measures at the LCK coastline, to enable our farms to be climate resilient.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I hope Members will look out for the exhibition when it is finally launched.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In the East Johor Strait shown on the slide, which is separated by the Causeway from the West Johor Strait, we have a distinct and separate cluster of fish farms, supported by key aquaculture facilities.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The separation of the fish farms into two distinct clusters is especially important to enhance fish resiliency in the face of climate change, which may result in harmful algal blooms as has happened in the past before.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Miss Cheryl Chan and Prof Koh Lian Pin asked how aquaculture would contribute to our "30 by 30" goal.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Prof Koh Lian Pin also asked how we would ensure that the development of aquaculture in sea spaces is environmentally sustainable.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We have identified fish production as one of our priority areas.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is a nutritious source of protein that can be grown efficiently.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is why we launched the Singapore Aquaculture Plan last year, to transform the sector in three ways.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: First, to increase and optimise spaces for farming.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And thirdly, to invest in research and innovation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SFA will also dedicate significant resources and work closely with industry and academics to enhance our understanding of the effects of aquaculture on our local marine environment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, SFA is collaborating with NUS and the Barramundi Group to study the impact of aquaculture on the marine environment and marine life surrounding St John’s Island.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The study will conduct reef surveys and measure water and sediment quality prospectively over a period of time, to better understand in real-time, how aquaculture practices and farming activities could potentially affect these environmental parameters.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will adopt relevant practices from our overseas learning trip and detailed insights gained from our own local studies to suit our Singapore context.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To further support Singapore's ambitions in leading aquaculture research and innovation, we will enhance our R&D facilities to attract more companies and researchers to base themselves here.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The brain trust of AquaPolis will comprise scientists from various research institutions, including the National University of Singapore (NUS), Temasek Life Sciences Laboratory and many others.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They will work on addressing real world aquaculture challenges to enhance the productivity of farms and quality of fish farmed in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, by developing superior fingerlings with traits, such as faster growth rates and higher Omega-3 content and reducing fish mortality from common fish diseases.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SFA's Marine Aquaculture Centre, located on St John's Island, will serve as the anchor research campus of AquaPolis.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: First, we will enhance its facilities with upgrades, such as the installation of recirculating aquaculture systems for research in intensive farming within closed environments, to cater to evolving R&D needs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Second, we will also embark on a study to review how our future research facilities can be better integrated with aquaculture infrastructure, such as jetties and hatcheries.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In the steady state, our Singapore Aquaculture Plan will comprise three distinct centres, as you can see on the slide: the West Johor Strait, the East Johor Strait and AquaPolis in the Southern Waters.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will provide critical diversification of our aquaculture production across three different sites and ensures our aquaculture sector expands in a climate-resilient manner.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The enhanced research capabilities and facilities will also be better integrated with aquaculture infrastructure.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked about plans to build the manpower pipeline for our farming industry.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For students, Republic Polytechnic has broadened the scope of their Diploma in Biotechnology to include a specialisation in Food and Agro-technologies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will provide them with engineering skills to operate new agriculture and aquaculture systems, knowledge about food crops cultivation and fish farm management.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will, therefore, have training programmes for different segments of the workforce to meet the agri-food industry's manpower needs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As we encourage our local farms to produce more, there must be sufficient demand for our local produce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I agree that this is an area we should study further.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In February, a new Alliance for Action (AfA) on "Demand Offtake and Consumer Education" was formed, as part of the Forward Singapore conversation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The AfA includes key members of our local food ecosystem, such as representatives from farms, off-takers, such as supermarkets and trade associations representing the hotels, the retailers, as well as the catering associations, supported by various agencies, like Singapore Tourism Board (STB) and Enterprise Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Together, they will explore solutions to help the hotel, restaurants and catering sector, as well as our local consumers, embrace local produce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I look forward to hearing their ground up recommendations that will further develop our local agricultural industry.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: (In Mandarin):   Food is an existential concern for Singapore as we import more than 90% of our food supply.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Over the past two years, we have experienced first-hand the effects of disruption to our food supply chain.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Many consumers have readily embraced alternatives, for example, by buying thawed frozen chickens from Australia and Thailand, or by switching to other protein types, such as fish and eggs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To ensure the continuous growth of local agriculture, the next key step is to grow demand for local produce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In February, a new Alliance for Action (AfA) on "Demand Offtake and Consumer Education" was formed, as part of the ForwardSG conversation, including representatives from farming, food processing, hospitality and F&B sectors.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: AfA will look into demand and supply aggregation of local produce and build greater mindshare for local produce through consumer education.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Recommendations from AfA will strengthen our food supply resilience.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The development of our agriculture industry depends on the support from Singaporeans for our local produce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: (In English): Ms Nadia Samdin asked how SFA will innovate to bolster its food safety capabilities.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SFA is developing Whole Genome Sequencing analytics to better identify the causes of foodborne diseases, and to help prevent outbreaks.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will strengthen SFA's use of data analytics to identify food establishments with higher risks of food safety lapses, enabling our officers to conduct more targeted inspections and educate poorer performing food establishments to tighten their food safety practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will also invest in deep technology to ensure that our food safety regime keeps pace with industry innovation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Dr Lim Week Kiak about progress in novel foods.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SFA will support research projects to develop new methodologies which aim to provide more timely assessments, including toxicity and allergenicity assessments for novel and alternative proteins.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Home-based food businesses are not licensed by SFA as they pose relatively low food safety risks due to their small scale.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They are still subjected though to prevailing food safety regulations and should comply with SFA's regulations and guidelines on proper food handling practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In January, a new Singapore Standard was launched to guide food e-commerce players on their roles and responsibilities related to food safety.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The guidelines were co-developed with a wide range of stakeholders, from food e-commerce platforms to food delivery platforms as well as supermarket retailers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I am heartened to see strong industry support in committing towards best practices in providing food safety information to consumers and improving traceability and recall along the food e-commerce chain.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Next, I will touch on coastal and flood protection, which Dr Lim Wee Kiak, Mr Edward Chia, Ms Nadia Samdin as well as Ms Poh Li San asked about.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Thirty percent of our land area is less than five metres above the mean sea level.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: With climate change, the Centre for Climate Research Singapore estimates that the mean sea level around Singapore could increase by up to one metre by 2100.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will affect many stretches of our coastline.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Combined with the effects of more sudden and extreme rainfall as well as storm surges, we can expect greater risks to the community, our infrastructure, and our livelihood.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: PUB, our national coastal protection agency, has been making steady progress and will periodically refine our coastal protection plans.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To Mr Edward Chia's question, since May 2021, we have progressively launched several studies to understand the characteristics of Singapore's coastlines and develop targeted coastal protection measures.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I agree with Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Ms Nadia Samdin that these present opportunities to shape climate resilience efforts with the public.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In conjunction with the Forward Singapore exercise, PUB started the Our Coastal Conversation series, and conducted two dialogue sessions for the City-East Coast area in October 2022.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Participants from diverse backgrounds, corporates, community groups, NGOs and even schools, participated in the dialogue and raised interesting perspectives on the trade-offs that we would need to make to tackle the effects of climate change.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, some participants raised issues like, how would we retain the scenic views and the convenient access to the beaches that we enjoy while, at the same, looking at how we protect our coastlines, including the coastal nature parks.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Last year, we published Singapore's first National Action Strategy on Marine Litter in consultation with our people, public and private sectors.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will establish a vibrant R&D ecosystem to support the development of innovative coastal protection and flood management solutions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I agree with Prof Koh Lian Pin that we should work with industry and consider solutions that they can offer.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The CFRP’s applied research and living lab components will support the test-bedding of inter-disciplinary urban flood solutions and equip our industries with the capability to develop and eventually export the next generation of coastal and flood protection solutions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: More details will be provided later this year.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Beyond sea level rises, climate change will also bring about increased and more intense rainfall, as we experienced in the last two days.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ms Nadia Samdin, Ms Poh Li San and Mr Edward Chia asked about drainage and coastal protection infrastructure plans.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Edward Chia also asked about how these will be financed.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We have set aside another $1.4 billion to carry out further improvements to the drainage system from 2021 to 2025.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Drainage improvement works in 25 locations are currently ongoing, including the expansion of the Bukit Timah Canal.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: PUB is exploring solutions that address the combined effects of sea level rise and intense rainfall and will continue to collaborate with agencies to co-create multi-functional drainage solutions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But the cost to expand our drainage to cater for every extreme rainfall event is prohibitive.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We must therefore strengthen our community resilience and collective response to how we deal with floods.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I encourage everyone to stay updated on PUB's flood alerts.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Please sign on to their Telegram alert system if you have not done so, and for property owners and developers to ensure that the flood protection measures in your own developments remain effective.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Chairman, as a small city-state with no natural resources, we must adapt and evolve to the constant changes around us.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will continue to strengthen our resilience against existential threats by reimagining our coastlines as we explore new coastal protection measures, improving our drainage infrastructure to withstand more intense rainfall, and building a more food resilient Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Whether it is mitigating the effects of climate change or strengthening our food resilience, each and every one of us has a role to play.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: My Ministry will work in partnership with all Singaporeans to build a more resilient Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Chairman, dengue continues to pose a serious threat to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In fact, this situation is also due to our success in tackling dengue over the decades.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In the sixties and seventies, dengue was prevalent and was a major cause of childhood death.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While we have significantly reduced the local population's exposure to the disease, it has also resulted in low population dengue immunity today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: That is why we must continue to step up efforts in the fight against dengue.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This includes one, surveillance of the Aedes  aegypti mosquito population and circulating dengue virus; two, working with premises managers and residents to eliminate mosquito breeding; and three, publicity campaigns and outreach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This includes the use of purple alert banners we introduced last year to inform residents of areas with high mosquito population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA also partners key stakeholders such as Town Councils in mosquito control efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, the Ministry of Health (MOH) and the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) monitor the development of and evaluate dengue vaccines and therapeutics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The evaluation of the TAK-003 vaccine, which Ms Sylvia asked about, is currently ongoing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While dengue cases have decreased from the peak in the middle of last year, weekly cases remain high, with the potential for another surge in cases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA has been leveraging technology to strengthen our existing dengue control regime.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One example is Project Wolbachia, where non-biting male Wolbachia-Aedes mosquitoes, are released at selected dengue high-risk areas to suppress the local mosquito population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To Ms Hany Soh, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Poh Li San’s queries on the progress of this pilot project, I am pleased to report that results thus far have been encouraging.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Initial studies have shown that continued releases of male Wolbachia-Aedes mosquitoes can successfully suppress the urban Aedes aegypti mosquito population in release sites.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: During the 2022 outbreak, the technology has prevented large clusters in these areas, where dengue transmission used to be high historically.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In the second half of last year, NEA expanded Project Wolbachia pilot to eight additional sites.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is part of a multi-site field study to further evaluate the impact of Wolbachia technology on dengue cases and clusters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Alongside HDB blocks, NEA has also been carrying out releases at landed residential estates to determine the most effective and impactful approach for wider-scale deployment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Based on early data, declining Aedes aegypti mosquito populations have also been observed in these areas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA will continue to collaborate with commercial partners to enhance automation and scale up both in-house and outsourced Wolbachia-Aedes mosquito production and release capacity to support the ongoing study.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to collect data for rigorous evaluation of the Wolbachia technology and to refine deployment and strategies to allow cost-effective expansion in the next few years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Regardless, the Wolbachia technology is not a silver bullet.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Profuse breeding of Aedes mosquitoes could reverse the success effected by the Wolbachia technology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NEA will continue to work with partner agencies and stakeholders to detect and remove potential mosquito breeding habitats and will take firm enforcement action where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our community must continue to play an active part in upkeeping our environment to prevent mosquito breeding and to curb transmission of the dengue virus.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is why NEA has been working closely with community partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, NEA collaborated with the West Coast and Pioneer grassroots organisations to tackle several large dengue clusters in the area last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Roadshows were organised to educate residents on measures to prevent mosquito breeding and to protect themselves from dengue.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Grassroots volunteers also conducted house visits and distributed educational flyers and insect repellent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Chairman, Minister Fu shared how the Government is leading our nation’s green transition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To succeed in our goal, we will need communities and individuals to step up and step forward.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are committed to partnering the community to foster a more liveable and sustainable society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is the only way for us to meet our climate goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The nationwide movement brings together community leaders and residents to plan, organise and co-implement sustainability initiatives in their communities to support the Singapore Green Plan.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked about the support and resources provided for GAC groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have held capacity workshops for GAC groups in all five districts and are rolling out localised deep dives where community leaders discuss in smaller groups to formulate plans that best meet the unique needs and conditions of their communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Residents and volunteers who are passionate about sustainability come together and are empowered to develop their own action plans to rally their communities and champion sustainability initiatives in their neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have also published a GAC guidebook for GAC groups to look for ideas, funding and partners for sustainability initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The workshops have been very fruitful with great ideas that meet the community’s needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, repairing, proper recycling of e-waste, composting of food waste, having a car-free day and more community involvement in tree-planting activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will embark on the next phase this year to galvanise community participation in the action plans and showcase some of the key programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Residents will be able to contribute their ideas and participate in the programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I hope we will see many more Community Eco-Days and other green initiatives like what Ms Nadia Samdin and her team have done.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through MSE's annual Climate Action Week (CAW), we have been working with our partners to encourage communities to take collective climate action towards a sustainable future for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are happy to see increasing participation from the People, Private and Public sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last year's CAW saw over 140 activities organised by 80 partners; the highest numbers since its launch in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will better reflect the wide range of sustainability initiatives and programmes it encompasses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I urge our People, Private and Public sector partners to join this community movement and organise sustainability-related activities beyond just a week, to rally even more Singaporeans towards a sustainable lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: There will be a wide range of activities for everyone when Go Green SG is launched in early July this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Singaporeans can join international visitors in more lifestyle programming to learn more about sustainability through fun and meaningful immersive experiences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked about the SG Eco Fund and engaging youths to encourage more ground-up sustainability initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SG Eco Fund was launched in November 2020 to support ground-up solutions for a greener and more sustainable Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Among them, we have a group of students that are using food scraps to breed crickets as an ingredient for making pet food and a project to teach women from vulnerable backgrounds to upcycle unwanted clothing donations into useful items.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Golden Cap Farm, a local startup, will run a pilot progamme to collect used coffee grounds from cafes and re-use it as a substrate for growing mushrooms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They will also organise mushroom farm tours and composting workshops.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Social enterprise, Two Glasses, is raising awareness about the impact of fast fashion and overconsumption through its short films and community discussions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They are also developing a counter for people to track new clothing purchased and the number of times they wear each piece of clothing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These aim to encourage a shift in behaviour of overconsumption.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Just from this sampling of projects, we see ideas for food waste used to produce food for either humans or pets and those that evolve around the clothes we wear, stop excessive buying and up-cycle unwanted clothes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The range of topics covered by them will help to move us towards our climate and Green Plan goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: More importantly, we see that grant recipients come from all walks of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Prof Koh Lian Pin pointed out, there are various funding schemes besides the SG Eco Fund that enable communities to take action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Each scheme is designed to encourage action with varying thematic or stakeholder considerations and is assessed accordingly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As what Prof Koh said so well: "Everyone from every sector has important contributions to make." We need everyone to work together towards a sustainable Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With the various funding support schemes available, we hope that whether you are young or old, an individual or an organisation, you can all play a part to build our green nation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We all have a shared responsibility in achieving our climate goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We must come together as a nation to work towards this important and urgent matter.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I urge all Singaporeans to join forces on climate action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We must act together now for a greener and more sustainable Singapore.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: I have one question for Minister Grace Fu.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: She mentioned that Pandan Reservoir will also be expanded to include the floating solar farms.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: I have another question for Senior Minister of State Koh.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: I am heartened to learn about the set-up of the Coastal Protection and Flood Management Research Programme (CFRP) to have an applied research and living lab in NUS.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: And the last question is for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: In the fight against dengue, I understand that to expand Project Wolbachia, we have to increase mosquito productions from two million to five million every week.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: How do we sustain this effort over the long run?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Chairman, I would like to thank Ms Poh for her clarifications.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is important for us to take a holistic evaluation on the impact on the environment, and Members, as well as members of the public, can rest assured that PUB will do the right thing of studying before we embark on it.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We had taken care of it when we did Tengeh, situating the solar panels where we are limiting the size, where we think that it is appropriate for the animals and the birds in the area.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will similarly do the same for Pandan Reservoir.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Plus, there will be an executive committee that comprises some of the experts in this related fields that provide insights and opinions on how best to scale up and grow this particular organisation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, with the involvement of more industry partners as well as other IHLs, there will be opportunities then for students in these institutions to involve in some of the R&D work.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That is how we build up the talent pipeline.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Connections with other international bodies of excellence would then also create another network where we can bring expertise from overseas to scale up and boost the expertise on R&D.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we need to see how we are able to do this in a cost-effective way, with the large-scale production and release of these mosquitoes in these public areas.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But at the same time, before that, we must also determine scientifically how effective this technology that is being rolled out and whether it is effective at a large scale, across the whole of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We need to look at the dynamics of the Wolbachia mosquitoes with the wild-type mosquitoes out there, how they survive, how they continue to find the female mosquitoes to mate.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: And also, how they are released and distributed across the dense urban setting we have in Singapore, both high-rise HDB blocks, including 50 storeys that we have and that we are building, as well as landed property estates.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We need to justify that we are able to use our resources prudently in a cost-effective way so that we can achieve the desired outcome.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I would like ask for Members' patience as NEA, with the Environmental Health Institute, work on studying the different roll-outs that we have so far, establishing the scientific basis of the effectiveness and also getting the resources to scale up production accordingly.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
text: I think it makes a lot of sense to attract the best people and best organisations here quickly, to support us.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
text: At the same time, I would like to hear the Minister's thoughts on what more can we do.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
text: How can we ensure that there is sufficient investment and coordination across our public, private and people sectors to nurture world-class sustainability champions, leaders and institutions of our own, to service both Singapore and the global community?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Chairman, I thank Prof Koh Lian Pin for a very thoughtful question.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I totally agree with him about the need to create excellence in Singapore but at the same time have a strong local anchor so that Singaporeans will find exciting career and also will be able to create value as we move towards sustainability.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It also intends to pull in disciplines from other centres that are related to coastal protection and flood management.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, if we consider nature-based solutions, then expertise in this area will have to be incorporated.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At the same time, we talked about a living lab where interesting solutions that have worked elsewhere, we need to refine, we need to test and we need to pilot it, to ensure that they are effective in the Singapore context.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is where overseas expertise and local companies can jointly work on such projects, and therefore, anchoring, transferring and absorbing some of these foreign expertise into the local talent pool.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is both vertical, like coastal protection; and horizontal, cutting across sustainability, verification and management reporting of carbon emissions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, there are many opportunities and lots of work ahead of us, and we want to see how we can bring greater coordination between the public, private and people sectors.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: The first one is for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: But the challenge will be for the many people who are out there, they will now think, are the hawkers now profiteering as a result of it?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I believe most hawkers are not and they are just trying to earn a decent living.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Can Senior Minister of State Khor share a little bit more.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Apart from what we already know, how we can ensure that price increase of cooked food in future does not outpace the inflation rate that is in the market?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: For all the cooked-food stalls that are under the direct rental with NEA, will NEA consider asking them to at least provide a budget meal in some form or the other, even though they are not the Socially-conscious Enterprise Hawker Centres?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: The second clarification is for Senior Minister of State Khor.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I am very heartened that she shared all the plans for the aquaculture.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: They are very good because they consider all the different aspects within the ecosystem.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: But as we all know, R&D efforts also take time to translate into commercialisation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The main operating cost is the cost of food ingredients.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is about 57% and then the next is manpower cost.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, we do have we do have rentals at $2 a month.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For our new Socially-conscious Enterprise Hawker Centres (SEHCs), we have a staggered rental scheme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, for the first two years, the stallholders do not pay the full rental.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is 80%, 90%; and then, in the third year 100%.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: During the pandemic, and even during repairs and redecoration works, if disruptions are over a prolonged period, we give rental waivers and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And we also give rebates for S&CC and so on, when centres are closed for upgrading.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is how we try and keep the rentals reasonable and not speculative, to help the hawkers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I hope that that helps to clarify that when I say rental is 9%, it does not mean the hawkers are profiteering because there are other costs involved, which are even higher.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to asking whether for existing hawker stalls which are tendered out, do we then want to ask them to provide budget meals?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Actually, our survey showed even now, prices of hawker food in our hawker centres are generally lower than those in the other comparable food establishments within the vicinity, like coffee shops and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And indeed, whilst you asked this, there are some people who perceive that SEHC hawker food is higher priced.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But, basically, when you look at it, they are comparable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think that competition would help, because hawkers will price according to what they think the market can take – the patron demographics, as well as their cost structure, the location and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our surveys have shown that they are reasonable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Singh also asked whether we can build one in Marina Bay because he thinks that the hawker centres' hawker food is much more reasonable.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: First, I must say that our "30 by 30" goal, is a stretch target.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Today, we import 90% of the food we consume, so we do have a lot of headroom that we need to make up for.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Unfortunately, the two years of COVID-19 disruption has also caused many of our farm projects to be delayed, especially those who are in the midst of trying to start their construction in the midst of COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Delays in raw materials, delay in supplies, curtailment of work by foreign workers unable to work because of COVID-19 – all these have caused at least about one to two years of delay in the implementation plan.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But when you talk to the farming community, they are committed to try and increase the production, and increase our food resilience.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As I said in my speech, what is important also is to make sure that as they produce more, Singaporeans are prepared to consume more of local produce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There must be a demand for the produce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Many of our farmers actually can produce more, but they have hesitancy doing so, not knowing whether the market can absorb the produce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Which is why I think it is important for all of us to buy our collective insurance – we need to support more local produce, so that you give a signal and encouragement to our farmers to do more production.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In reaching our "30 by 30" target – which is a stretch goal, as I said – but it is also a journey.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think we are trying our very best, resourcing our farmers with funding, helping them with technology adoption.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We have seen some early success of this, where some of our fish farms, for example, are taking on more productive methods using recirculating aquaculture systems: floating on the sea, rather than just using the seawater as it is, but filtering and actually creating a more conducive environment within the tanks for the fish to be grown in a more dense manner, yet kept in a very safe and very humane way to allow the tonnage to be much more intense.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And I think if more of our farms adopt such productive technologies, we will be closer to hitting our "30 by 30" target.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But for vegetables and fish, we do need more Singaporeans to support consumption, so that we can ramp up.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And the Alliances for Action (AfA) that we have just announced will, hopefully, be able to shape our consumers and our B2B relationship with our farms to increase off-take and increase consumption, so that together, we build ourselves towards that resilience we desire.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Could I ask whether we have a timeline in terms of when we will expand the green procurement practices and the disposable bag charge?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And whether the Ministry will consider publishing a roadmap for these expansions, similar to what we have done for our carbon tax?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, I am sure Senior Minister of State Amy Khor did not do this on purpose, but she did not respond to my cuts on second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Could I ask her whether we can do a public consultation or set up a citizens workgroup to tackle this issue of second-hand smoke?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Chairman, we expected Mr Louis Ng to ask "what's next?", even as and when we announce the first step.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I would just like to assure Members that we would definitely want to go as fast as possible.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Focusing on our target of 2030 and realising that green procurement has its impact of expanding the introduction of new, more environmentally friendly products and services; and also, hopefully, as a pathfinder, introduce more technologies and introducing scale, so that we can help to bring down the costs of such products and services.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we are very mindful about the impact that we can play.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But at the same time, I think several Members in the House, Mr Chairman, have also asked that we do it in a way that is inclusive, so that all our companies, our SMEs are also brought along this journey.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Balancing the pace is a bit like the Goldilocks problem – not too hot, not too cold, just right.
