speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We should not go too slowly, but neither should we go too quickly, but we should do it just right.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will take the lessons learned from the first tranche that we will be implementing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: You are talking about small little bags, why do you need to use it?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Put in the pocket, put in the bag, your handbag and so on, and you do not actually need.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, the idea is to nudge a change in behaviour.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If indeed, once we start this, there is a significant change in behaviour, then there is no need to expand it because people will change their behaviour automatically, they will not take the bags if they do not need to.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And also, other organisations may follow suit in charging for bags just to help nudge behaviour.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, I think we need to monitor and do not jump the gun.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I also want to thank the Member for asking a clarification on second-hand smoke.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And it was not my pet subject, so I had to choose.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Yes, but thank you, now I can continue with the rest of my speech.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng was suggesting setting up a citizens workgroup to study this issue of second-hand smoke in homes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The key challenge in this matter is in enforcing against second-hand smoke in homes, if we want to do it.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And the challenges are, as we have already said, but I will repeat it again: technological constraints and privacy concerns, to collect clear and Court-admissible evidence of smoking in homes, whether it is at the balconies or windows, and by identifiable individuals.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, I think we cannot resolve this issue simply by just setting up a citizens workgroup, in order to get the group to discuss about the issue of second-hand smoke.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But as I have said before, and it is worth repeating again – we are monitoring technologies in this area to see whether we can utilise anything to strengthen enforcement possibilities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And many other legislative and policy measures that we put in.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If we reduce smoking prevalence, the second-hand tobacco smoke issue will also be addressed.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I have three supplementary questions, two is for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I am heartened to hear about the plans to be rolled out on the International E-Waste Day, which is in October.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: But apart from that, could NEA also look into how the three Ps can come together, to increase awareness in other aspects.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: For example, the World Environment Day in June, and coming up very soon, the Global Recycling Day on 18 March, so that we can encourage more active recycling and for the community to collectively take the lead to further reduce the contamination rate of our recyclables.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: The second question is on the charging for plastic bags.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: During Marsiling-Yew Tee GRC's Green Action Communities deep dive, one of the suggestions is actually to explore how the community can collaborate with supermarkets to incentivise and encourage Bring Your Own Bag (BYOB) initiatives.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: So, how can the Ministry facilitate to link up the community and these supermarkets, so as to organise more of such green sustainable initiatives.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Thirdly, for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey, in relations to the Project Wolbachia, I understand that it has been rolled out and it is intended to ramp up to more HDB blocks and also landed homes.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Can I also clarify that whether we are also exploring, if we have sufficient numbers, to release it to the private condominiums as well, as during the peak periods.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: For example, in Wood Grove, I have seven condominiums, there is actually a cluster for these condominiums.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, we can work with the grassroots, the local advisors, as well as to via the Green Action for Communities programme, which Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey was talking about, in order to look at outreach and education efforts, as well as increasing awareness about recycle and nudging people to adopt such green habits.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have got our NEA officers on the ground too, and we can work to this as well as through the Green Action for Communities programme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And one of them could be giving out reusable bags to the community, to encourage them to use that.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: And we will need to work with the Management Corporation Strata Titles (MCSTs) because we need access to the premises.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we will need such a collaboration with MCSTs and the condominium residents.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Let us take one step at a time; but certainly, the condominium residents would be on our radar screen as well.

speaker: Mr Chairman
text: Mr Louis Ng, you may wish to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It covers the food we eat, the environment we live in, the water we drink and, of course, the future of humankind, in terms of protecting our planet and fighting climate change.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And I did not forget and did not run out of time – the air we breathe, second-hand smoke as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I know I ask some difficult questions, especially to Senior Minister of State Amy, but since she says she is immune to it, we can continue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But I want to record my sincere appreciation for the hard work by all the office holders, the team and staff members at MSE, NEA, PUB, SFA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: For again, ending the use of disposable cups, for turning up the air-con temperature, so we sweat it out as we debate here – all in the spirit of cutting our emissions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
